searchText: <@740537964131647528> Merkle Tree PR looks good! If you are planning on moving onto PMT, I'd suggest to make it brief and avoid the idiosyncrasies of PMT. There's quite a bit of complexity involved with VT 😄 https://github.com/herumi/mcl <@427491045308235776> can this library be used to implement the cryptography needed for Verkle Trees? Checked it and it has components like bigint, but it would require a bit of hand-grease to make it work. in terms of requirements, which parts of the cryptography do you not want to implement? i cant find any lib in C# that implements the primitives to implement any kind of elliptic curve, I don't want to start from scratch implementing the basic elliptic curve operations. one strategy is to implement an unoptimised version with the BigInt equivalent in CSharp, I can help with this, then replace it later on with C bindings Oh scratch that then 😄 I'm guessing that all of the existing nethermind ECC code uses bindings then? there are libraries for ECC we need right now, and they are in turn bindings we have UInt256/Int256 implemented for C# What about binding to the ECC library in rust via C? (arkworks for example has bandersnatch, then you can add the safety layer (banderwagon) in c# or you can bind to banderwagon directly Yeah this is all you need to implement it from scratch, though I can see why you would not want to do this as its a fair amount of cryptography less the verkle trie cryptography needed Let me know what your appetite is and I'll be happy to assist yes, that's why I didn't want to do it. Also I would have to explore a lot to understand how to do the implementation part. that is what I am working on currently - but i thought if i can find something in c/c++ it would be easier to interop. if i am up for implementing something from scratch, where should I start? I guess want you want initially in the bindings is something like: ``` // Point methods point_add(left : &Point, right : &Point, result : &mut Point) point_double(x : &Point, result : &mut Point) multi_scalar_mul(scalars : &[Field], points : &[Point], result : &mut Point) // Scalar Methods field_add(left : Scalar, right : &Scalar, result : &mut Scalar) field_sub(left : Scalar, right : &Scalar, result : &mut Scalar) field_mul(left : Scalar, right : &Scalar, result : &mut Scalar) field_inv(x : &Scalar, result : &mut Scalar) field_neg(x : &Scalar, result : &mut Scalar) ``` Then you would mainly only need to implement the banderwagon and verkle trie cryptography I wrote an implementation in python from scratch, I'll push local changes and then link it okay, thanks for the help! Added a section in the readme to specify the order that you should implement things in: https://github.com/crate-crypto/verkle-trie-ref#cryptography-modules (All modules contain tests, so you can see exactly where your impl and the deviates from the python impl) In general optimisations are removed, so it _should_ be easier to read thats great, thanks! will start on it right away and reach out if I need some help 😄 thanks! yea I've realised it's a tall ladder from Earth to verkle trees 😅

excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
I guess want you want initially in the bindings is something like:

```
// Point methods
point_add(left : &Point, right : &Point, result : &mut Point)
point_double(x : &Point, result : &mut Point)
multi_scalar_mul(scalars : &[Field], points : &[Point], result : &mut Point)

// Scalar Methods
field_add(left : Scalar, right : &Scalar, result : &mut Scalar)
field_sub(left : Scalar, right : &Scalar, result : &mut Scalar)
field_mul(left : Scalar, right : &Scalar, result : &mut Scalar)
field_inv(x : &Scalar, result : &mut Scalar)
field_neg(x : &Scalar, result : &mut Scalar)
```

Then you would mainly only need to implement the banderwagon and verkle trie cryptography
